Ransomware is so easy to deal with. At home format and restore files from your last backup. At work well take that Disaster Recovery plan and implement it.

If you don't have backups you will loose at least part of your data at some point either to virus or just a drive failure; computers are like cars backing up is putting in gas, changing the tires between winter and summer tires is dusting, and having the whole engine serviced is replacing the drive and doing a format every 3-5 years.

Computers are more complex then your TV/Radio and as such require a bit more care back up your files monthly, take canned air to the fans and vents every six months and expect after 5 years to do a full wipe and replace drives and it can last you a long time if you just browse the web if you do more the 5 year step may be a new PC for an upgrade. This is for home. If you are at work those backups need to be weekly or daily depending on your business, and they need to go offsite (that means far enough that a tornado won't take out both if it makes a B-line from one to the other).
Thanks for sharing your knowledge. I think I'll clean my computer when I unpack it.
Note: Have manual backups stored apart from the scheduled backups. If you get ransom ware and then your system is backed up, your back up will be no good.
